correctness.rationale: The R3 radial Fourier integral is 8pi*a/([(a^2+(omega-s)^2)(a^2+(omega+s)^2)]). The Bessel dimension walk has the exact factor -4pi*d/d(s^2), so in d=2p+1 the density equals ((4pi)^p(p-1)!/omega) Im[(s^2+(a-i omega)^2)^(-p)]. Its phase beta decreases strictly from 2 atan(omega/a) to 0; the density is nonnegative at all frequencies iff 2p atan(omega/a)<=pi. Negative open bands establish necessity; Bochner and positive spectral density on s>0 establish sufficiency and distinct-site strictness. Algebraic identities checked by verify.py; no finite sample used as proof.

value.rationale: The wave/sinc covariance arises canonically as the inverse Fourier transform of a spherical frequency shell, and exponential damping is a natural regularization. Unlike the trivial R3 product-closure fact, the complete family of sharp positive-definiteness thresholds in higher odd dimensions determines when damping recovers admissible covariance models, identifies all negative Fourier bands outside them, and supplies exact boundary behavior and distinct-site strictness. The dimension-five and higher cutoffs are not textbook corollaries of product closure alone.
